THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County supervisors punted on the Hub City Wind project while adopting new rules on battery storage and data centers; Wausau's Finance Committee meanwhile advanced funding for a downtown development and wrestled with lead-pipe replacement costs.

  • Marathon County Board referred the Hub City Wind resolution back to the Executive Committee after debate over the county's limited authority under state PSC jurisdiction, with a new recommendation due in September.
  • The County Board adopted a 500-foot setback rule for battery energy storage systems and passed a temporary moratorium on new data centers, with both ordinances taking immediate effect.
  • Wausau's Finance Committee approved a tax increment revenue bond for the Foundry on Third development and adopted a four-session budget workshop calendar beginning October 5.
  • Wausau's Board of Public Works approved roughly $1.2 million in pay estimates for lead service line replacement and Stark Street construction, and selected Clark Dietz for a sanitary sewer capacity study.
  • Weston's Parks Committee heard a concept for a 30,000-square-foot indoor community space at Kennedy Park from Everest Youth Hockey, green-lighting further feasibility work with no village funding committed.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on accepting the Village Clerk's resignation at a special meeting called for August 27.

Coming up: Wausau's Committee of the Whole meets Wednesday, September 2, likely to take up items advanced from this week's Finance and Rules Review committees; the city's Economic Development Committee meets Tuesday, September 1, at 5:30 p.m.
